newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Arab youths killed by West Bank landmine.
newsitem.headline: Two Arab youths killed by West Bank landmine.

text.p: Two 13-year-old Palestinian boys were killed on Thursday by a landmine explosion in the West Bank, PLO security officials said.

The Israeli military issued a statement that appeared to suggest the youths, killed near the cemetery of their village of Anza, were blown up by mines which might have been part of a guerrilla stockpile.
"According to the assessment of (Israeli) explosives experts, the mines were brought to the cemetery and were not planted in the ground," the army said.
"The mines are not of the type used by the Israeli army but have been used in the past by the Jordanian army," it said. "The reason why the mines were there is being investigated."
The West Bank was last a battlefield between the two armies in the 1967 Middle East war, when Israel captured the region from Jordan.

PLO security officials said Mohammad a-Barahmah and Nimr Jarrar found a landmine while playing near the cemetery, in an area of the West Bank where Israel has overall security control under peace deals with the PLO.
It exploded as they were handling it, killing them. Two other boys were wounded in the blast, the officials said.
On Saturday, an Islamic militant was killed in the same area of the West Bank when explosives he was handling detonated, PLO officials said.

Israeli security forces have been on high alert for weeks, fearing attempts by the Islamic Jihad guerrilla group to avenge the killing of its leader Fathi Shqaqi in Malta on October 26, 1995. Palestinians believe Israel carried out the assassination.
